newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stks end record-breaking streak, close off.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stks end record-breaking streak, close off.

text.p: Caracas stocks ended their eighth straight session record-breaking streak, closing off in heavy trade as local investors took profits, traders said.
But the upward trend that saw the bolsa rise some 35 percent in June is here to stay, they added.
"Good Venezuelan news keeps on coming ... so I'm sure the rise will continue," Union broker Hector Perez said.
June inflation data released Tuesday showed a deceleration of inflation to 1.8 percent, compared to 3.1 percent in May and 7.1 percent last year, beating market expectations of around 2.6 percent.
The market's 19-share index slipped 2.6 percent to end at 9,032.83 points as 405 million shares traded, worth 21 billion bolivars ($43 million), according to preliminary figures from the exchange.
"The profit-taking was mostly by locals -- you could see that because the sell orders were relatively small. Foreign buyers were not selling," Perez added.
Merinvest's composite index, which includes telephone company CANTV, meanwhile also dropped 2.6 percent to 141.14 points. Among traded shares, 34 fell, five rose and six closed flat.
